title: IB Global Politics Past Papers: Final-Weeks Plan
summary: IB Global Politics past papers become more useful with timed attempts, markscheme reviews, error logs and focused revision during the final weeks.
body_markdown:
The final weeks before an IB Global Politics exam are the time to turn what you know into marks. Archived exam questions help when you use a feedback loop: attempt, mark, diagnose, repair and repeat. Completing papers without examining your decisions can preserve the same weaknesses.


One detail matters for current students: the revised Global Politics course has its first assessment in 2026. Older material can develop source analysis, argumentation and evaluation, but its structure may not match your assessment. Prioritize current-format specimen material and check tasks against the latest course requirements.


### Your final-weeks checklist


Use this cycle for each practice session:


- Complete a paper or focused question set without notes.
- Mark it using the relevant markscheme.
- Separate knowledge gaps from reasoning and timing errors.
- Repair one recurring weakness.
- Retest it with a different question.


RevisionDojo's[IB Global Politics resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-global-politics) support this process. Use the Questionbank for targeted practice, then Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat and grading tools to address what each attempt reveals.


### Begin with a timed diagnostic


A diagnostic should show what you can produce independently. Put away your notes, follow the assessment time limit and continue even when an example refuses to appear.


For the course first assessed in 2026, Paper 1 lasts 1 hour 15 minutes at SL and HL. Its four compulsory source-based questions total 25 marks. Paper 2 lasts 1 hour 45 minutes, requires one response from each of two sections and totals 30 marks. HL students also sit Paper 3, a 1 hour 30 minute stimulus-based assessment worth 28 marks.


If conceptual connections feel uncertain, review the[IB Global Politics framework](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-the-framework-of-global-politics) before your next attempt. During the diagnostic, record missing knowledge briefly and keep writing. That note gives your next study session a purpose.


### Self-mark with evidence


Self-marking works when you assess the response on the page rather than the answer you intended to write. A markscheme is neither a transcript nor a complete model answer, so read its instructions carefully.


Ask whether you addressed the command term, used sources precisely, explained the political significance of evidence and sustained an argument. Check whether competing perspectives receive consideration and whether the conclusion reaches a reasoned judgement.


Annotate where marks were earned or missed. For uncertain decisions, return to the criteria. RevisionDojo's[guide to official questions and worked solutions](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/where-to-find-ib-past-papers-worked-solutions) explains why assessment materials need to be relevant and reliable.


Grading tools can offer another perspective on unclear reasoning or unsupported assertions. Use that feedback alongside the official criteria, and ask a teacher or tutor when a judgement remains unresolved.


A student discovers that the weak topic is hidden inside a filing cabinet of everything they confidently skipped


### Build an error log that changes tomorrow


A score describes an attempt. An error log determines what happens next.


Separate mistakes into three categories:


- **Knowledge:** missing case studies, inaccurate terminology or weak conceptual understanding.
- **Reasoning:** unsupported claims, one-sided analysis or examples disconnected from the argument.
- **Execution:** misread command terms, poor source integration or unfinished answers.


For each entry, record the task, exact weakness, repair action and retest date. “Revise human rights” is vague. “Compare two perspectives on humanitarian intervention and sovereignty, then write a timed paragraph” gives you something concrete to complete.


Look for patterns across attempts. Repeated weak conclusions suggest one recurring skill problem. Reusing a single case study may expose limited evidence. Choose[focused Global Politics self-study resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-ib-global-politics-resources-self-study) that address the pattern instead of rereading everything.


### Repair knowledge through retrieval and application


Close your materials and recall a weak topic from memory: concepts, actors, contrasting perspectives and usable examples. Check your Study Notes afterwards and fill the gaps. Turn stubborn details into Flashcards, or use AI Chat to test your explanation from another perspective.


Then apply what you repaired. Write a paragraph, plan an argument or answer a related source question. This checks whether you can select and use knowledge under pressure.


RevisionDojo's[guide to IB practice resources and AI study tools](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/effective-ib-practice-resources-ai-study-tools) can help match the resource to the weakness. The Coursework Library can offer examples of structured analysis, while Tutors can help when a problem survives several independent attempts. Keep your own exam responses original.


### Move towards full-paper control


Start with individual questions that isolate weaknesses. Combine tasks as those weaknesses improve, then complete current-format simulations to test timing, fatigue and question choice.


For Paper 2, reserve a short planning period. Define the debate, select evidence for competing claims and decide what judgement your conclusion will defend. For Paper 1, practise moving between source tasks without allowing one response to consume the available time.


HL students should also retrieve researched case studies for Paper 3 from memory. Organize each around the issue, actors, perspectives, evidence and analytical significance. Practise adapting that knowledge to unfamiliar stimuli.


The[RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) supports focused practice before longer sessions. Use Mock Exams and appropriately aligned Predicted Papers for additional rehearsal, checking that their format matches your course.


### Protect time for feedback in the final week


Alternate demanding attempts with repair sessions. Mark each timed paper while your reasoning is fresh, then address the two weaknesses most likely to affect several questions. Retest those weaknesses before adding another simulation.


In the final 24 hours, review your error log, core concepts, flexible case studies and timing plan. Avoid scheduling so much practice that feedback goes unused.


Each completed paper should change the next attempt. RevisionDojo brings practice, explanations and feedback together so you can keep that loop moving. The aim is to enter the exam knowing how to select evidence, build an argument and use the time available.
